Question: Have you ever overcome your stock market loss? How?
Answer: Have you ever overcome your stock market loss? How?: For a trader losses are like frequent unwanted guests. You are forced to meet and greet them and by the time they leave there is a hole in your pocket. There is no avoiding them but they need to be managed. There visits are to be kept to a minimum and expenses on them should be on a tight budget. Yes, I am talking about keeping the losses to a minimum. Easier said than done. Stock market losses are like guests overstaying and causing more financial stress. Well, like every other trader I too have seen some big losses. On most occasions, I have come through the situation reasonably well and back to profit making very soon. The first such instance occurred in January 2015 : The loss in the month was Rs. 127718. I had tried selling options this month because it is the conventional wisdom of the market. Little good it did to me. I was left licking my wounds. An introspection was required and done. One should do what one is good at. I was good at making money through buying options. I had gone for something which was not my strength. So decided to stick to option buying. This was the outcome in February 2015: Things worked out well and the loss from previous month was wiped out. Kept my faith in my trading methods and did more of the same over next month as well. Result for March 2015: There was a profit of Rs. 270242 at the end of the month for my humble efforts. Lessons Learnt : These are old trades but important to me for the following reasons: (1) I learnt that losses can be overcome by staying patient with your method. You just have to keep the belief. (2) Leave the profits to the market. Do not get out from a good trade in a hurry. (3) Trade as per your strength not what the others tell you to do. What Happened Next ? : With all the lessons learnt, I am still a human being. Humans make errors. I too made many of them and in November 2015 ( just 8 months later) was looking at a loss of Rs. 145000. December 2015 too ended in a loss of Rs. 10000. It took two more months with profits of Rs. 65000 and Rs. 166000 respectively in January and February 2016. Once again the losses could be erased and profitability restored. The year 2018 Loss : I share my stock selection and trades on OptionsNext. From May 2018, I posted about option buying trades. The first 3 months ended profitable. In August there was the visit by the unwanted guest— the big loss. Whether it was PUT buying or CALL buying, it was a losing proposition. The loss was Rs. 99589. In January 2015 I was a lonely trader like most traders are. it did not matter what I lost as no one else was involved. In August 2018, there were people reading my posts and some even taking the trades. They too lost money along with me. Every loss in the market is loss of credibility in the minds of the people with whom you are sharing the trades. You start doubting your methods. It was difficult but necessary to keep the belief. September 2018 : I kept doing what was normal. The crisis in ILFS and the crash in the markets on September 21, 2018 helped in a big way. The results were wonderful. A profit of Rs. 430609. The memories of the previous month were wiped away with the fortune smiling on my trades in September 2018. Subsequently October and November months too have been alright though nowhere near the heady high of September. Summary : I have shared my recovery from losses. The HOW part of the question is more important. The recovery was possible due to: Keeping the belief in my selection process and trading method. Trusting the market to give me the profit in the right trades. Knowing my losses in the wrong trades. Doing what I am supposedly good at i.e buying options even though the conventional wisdom is against it. The losses do create self doubts but if you are able to recover from the losses on multiple occasions by following the same set of rules that leads to self belief which is a trader’s most powerful asset. The discovery of this process in 2015 through the big loss experiences has been very good for me. I trust that the readers too will benefit from these experiences. It is always better to learn from the losses of others. Thanks for reading.

Question: What are the nonsense things stock market experts tell people?
Answer: What are the nonsense things stock market experts tell people?: Poor guys, these stock market experts. Doomed if they do not speak ( they are paid to speak ) and doomed if they speak and go wrong, which happens almost every time. They talk sense. Only market action after that turns the talk into nonsense. I stopped listening to these people sometime back but just watch them for few minutes once in a while to add some humour to my day. At times, the business channels are better than the Kapil Sharma Show. Only the jokes are on us but we find out later when we look at our account statements. I will list 3 nonsense things ( out of so many ) which come to mind immediately. (1) FII Buying and DII Selling Numbers: How does it matter to a person buying 5 shares of RELIANCE whether Foreign Institutional Investors are buying or whether LIC is selling. Will it make a difference if you bought a washing machine from the same showroom where Mukesh Ambani bought his washing machine? Just plain nonsense. If these institutions were so smart then 2008 would not have happened. Pramod Kumar's answer to How do I interpret the buy, sell, contracts and OI data of FII? (2) Reasons for the Market Action: It happens everyday. In the morning they talk about poor quarterly results of a company. They predict the stock prices to fall. Market opens and price is down 3%. Their viewpoint validated. Everyone is happy. Suddenly the stock recovers from the low point and ends the day up 7%. Poor results are still there and these experts now have to put a new spin on their morning theories to deal with the new situation. Speech is silver, silence is golden. But who will pay them to remain silent? Yesterday market went up due to the Rs. 2000000 crore stimulus package announcement. Part of that package was unveiled yesterday by the Finance Minister. Market may go down today. Nothing has changed. These people have to quickly come up with new nonsense. We shall be hearing that all day today. (3) Giving Undue Importance to Individuals: Basically these experts are selling the hype and not the expertise. Hype is generated by talking about Rakesh Jhunjhunwala and his buying into some stocks. How does that matter to you and me? They do not talk about his investments that go wrong like the recent one in YESBANK or earlier in Jaiprakash Associates. Hero worship is not expertise. When the appointment of Ravneet Gill as YESBANK CEO was confirmed by RBI in February 2019, these experts made a big song and dance of this news. The stock too shot up from Rs. 180 to Rs. 235 in a day and the party was on. These guys were predicting Rs. 350–400 zone once again. Selling the hype and hope. Ravneet Gill is still there, experts have moved on to different songs and learning new dances and YESBANK has come down to Rs. 28.00 level after making a low of Rs. 5.65 in March 2020. Just one year for the hope to be shattered and hype to be busted. These were my take on the nonsense things the experts talk about in the stock market. Now the bonus point: I have been writing on Quora for more than three years now. Mostly I write on stock market topics. I write a blog OptionNext too. Some people consider me also as a sort of expert though I beg to differ. You can consider what I just wrote as another nonsense thing from the one not so expert. Market deals with experts or the lay person in exactly same manner. It fools them all the time. Only experts get paid for the nonsense and others end up paying for it. Life goes on. Thanks for reading. Image : Google Images

Question: Are public sector bank stocks overvalued, undervalued, or correctly valued in Indian bourses?
Answer: Are public sector bank stocks overvalued, undervalued or correctly valued in Indian bourses?: Valuations are always subjective. What one person may consider undervalued may be overvalued for another. For a trade to take place there has to be an agreed price which is Market Price. Stock Market is the place where trades happen and market price decided. We are talking about Public Sector Banks today. I have written few answers earlier about these banks and nothing has changed to warrant a change in my opinion. Let us get there. In the past few years Government of India has pumped in lot of money into PSU Banks. The purpose was to keep them compliant with the RBI norms. In 2019, 10 PSU Banks were merged into 4. The same old theory —- Big banks, better business. It does not work like that in reality. If you merge 3 bad businesses you do not get 1 good business. The outcome is one very bad business. I have compared the stock prices after the 2017 recapitalization, 2019 recapitalization and mergers with the present stock prices of these banks. NIFTY, the benchmark index for the India market is up more than 40% since October 25, 2017. With the exception of SBIN, every other PSU Bank stock is trading at a much lower price. After the immediate bounce on the news, all of them fall back into their original trend. Dismal performance in a rising market. Just imagine what can happen when the market goes down. How are they valued?: We do not argue with the market. Market is always right. Yes, in short term, there are irrational prices but over a period of time, market puts the correct price on everything. Answer: Is stock market similar to gambling?: Maybe the daily fluctuations in prices and the resultant quick gains or losses makes it seem like gambling. Maybe the tale of woes of most traders and investors who lost money makes it seem like gambling. Or just because some people who know nothing about the market think that it is akin to gambling, we also start thinking in the same way. Let us consider these two facts: Keep gambling for a long time. There will be good gains in between to make it look worthwhile but finally there will surely be a loss. Money will be gone. Keep investing over a long period of time. There will be losses in between to make it look bad but finally there will surely be a gain. Money will be earned. To assert the second statement, it is the graph of NIFTY, the benchmark index since inception: There are crests and valleys in between. Those were the tough times in the market notably the year 2008 and the early part of this year. But those who stayed with their investments reaped the rewards. Does it look like gambling? Absolutely not. And it is not. I am one person who generally writes about the stocks which have proved worthless over a period of time, even over a long period of time. I am not easily taken in by the success stories of some stocks. For each success story, I can tell two horror stories about the stocks that crashed and never recovered. But even I will not dispute the fact that over a long period, stock market results generally outweigh any other kind of investment. We can not call that gambling. Question: Whether the sell in May and go away strategy for equity markets will hold good for May 2020 also, amidst already massive fall in global equity indices?
Answer: Sell in May and go away. Will it hold good for May 2020 also? The question implies that this strategy or saying actually worked in earlier years too. That premise is false. That assumption is wrong. The tussle between the bullish and bearish sentiment is always present in the market. Month of the year does not matter. At some point of time in the past, few May months might have shown a negative trend. That is how a catchy slogan is born. That is what it is and nothing more. That is not how one makes profit in the market and that is also not how losses are avoided. It is always prudent to check the facts. In Indian Stock Market, NIFTY is the index which represents the state of the market. I have checked the data for the month of May for 10 years — from 2010 to 2019. Compared NIFTY closing price on the first trading day of the month ( that is when you sell and go away ) with the closing price on the last day of the month. NIFTY closed negative for the month in the first 4 years from 2010 to 2013. From 2014 to 2019 ( 6 years ) , it is positive for the month. So there is no truth in the saying. Market moves are always random. We try to read too much into them unnecessarily. These kind of exercises never helped anybody make money in the market. Will it hold good this time? : For all we know, NIFTY may end up in the red for the month. It has not done that for last 6 times. So there is a likelihood just based on law of averages. So what? Nifty going up or down does not make money. Good trades and investments do. Let us keep our focus there and not lose our way chasing half baked and much hyped sayings which do not mean anything. Invest well, trade right in May and do not go away. Thanks for reading. Image : Google Images

Question: What do you think about the extension of lockdown by another two weeks up to May 17? Do you think it will be of help and economically viable?
Answer: Thanks for A2A Nagarajan sir. What do I think about extension of lock down till May 17?: Choice is between the devil and deep see. Choice is about dying from the virus or dying from hunger. Virus is present right now, hunger is waiting around the corner. Choice is not to be made by me. We have given that right to those whom we elected to run the governments. Choice made by the government may work out or may not work out because they are as clueless as you and me. Only they can not admit it. They are under constant scrutiny in these times of acute crisis and they have to be seen to be doing something. But what do you do when really there is no solution. You try many things by doing the minimum work required. The easy way was to extend the lock down. Government took that option. Will it help? : Probably. It will probably help in controlling the spread of the virus. On the other hand, the act of opening up certain activities may put paid to that hope. Suddenly we find trains running full of passengers going back to their villages. Even if a few stray cases carry the virus from the big urban cities to the villages of hinterland, we have a full blown crisis on our hands. Punjab is already seeing that effect with many pilgrims who returned from Huzoor Saheb, Nanded ( Maharashtra) were found positive. All that quarantine and isolation arrangements are putting additional pressure on the health and police personnel who are already working under tremendous strain. Extending the lock down and relaxing the norms is counter productive. But like I said earlier, it is not a choice that can be made easily. Will it be economically viable?: Absolutely not. Let us assume that lock down is lifted on May 17, 2020. We shall be happy that a burden has been lifted. That is all. Shall we go on outings as we used to do in the not so recent past? Shall we go to shopping malls and cinema? Will spectator sport events like cricket matches resume? Will anyone board a train to travel somewhere unless absolutely necessary? The corona virus has cast a sinister shadow on our lives and it will not go away soon. Even before the pandemic, we were talking about recession. Now it will be depression. No doubt that at some stage we shall come out of it. Human will finally triumphs over all adversities and it will do this time too. But the process will be long and painful. We have to bear with the pain. What we can do? : It is clear that our views do not matter at all in the bigger scheme of things. And the views of the high and mighty too do not matter in the God’s scheme of things. Whatever action we take will always be debatable because there are no yes/no type of solutions. Those of us who are fortunate enough that we do not worry about our daily earnings and loss of livelihood, can take care of one poor family for the duration of crisis. It will not be a big strain on our resources and a big help for those who need the help. We do not know how the government help is reaching the needy people but we shall be ensuring that at least a family of 3–5 persons is managing to eat and survive. The pandemic gives lot of power to the government to interfere in our choices and way of living. Not the right way a democracy should function. For a while, we can live with it but let us not lower the guard. Governments do not want to give up the control once they get it. That would be our social responsibility after the crisis is over. Till then, let us follow the guidelines. Let us get inspiration from this saying of Swami Vivekanand: Human will shall prevail. Thanks for reading.

Question: If JDU and TDP withdraw their support to BJP, shall the Modi 3.0 fall?

Why do we have to ask questions about the fall of a government even before it has taken oath? Is it pessimism or just passing time? Well, whatever it is, here are my two bits. Past governments lasting full term without majority: P V Narasimha Rao (1991–96), Atal Bihari Vajpayee (1999–2004) , Manmohan Singh ( 2004–2014) completed full terms as Prime Ministers while not enjoying a majority for their party. They all faced problems of withdrawal of support, no confidence motions, turmoil within the party in case of P V Narasimha Rao but the governments completed full terms. What is different now?: If these two gentlemen withdraw support? They may not do it immediately. Right now their concern is to get good bargain for their support. BJP will have to tackle these? Manmohan Singh was a political novice. Narasimha Rao and Vajpayee were masters in managing conflicting thought process. If all these people could manage to complete their full terms without having a majority in the Lok Sabha, present incumbent can surely do it. With 10 years of governance and facing a myriad of problems, Sh Narendra Modi is experienced enough to ride through any real or perceived crisis situation that may come up. It is not to say that Naidu or Nitish or both or any of the other allies will not ditch BJP at any time. Managing a coalition and running the government would be a humbling experience for the BJP. It is good for the party and good for the nation. For the present, let us look forward to swearing in of the new government. Nobody is withdrawing support anytime soon. I am not a fan of Mr Modi but would surely like to see him as Prime Minister once again. Question: Is it a good time to invest in bank stocks for the long term?
Answer: Is it a good time to invest in Bank Stocks for the long term ? : Banks are meant to be a profitable and good business. The business is simple. Get money from people at a cost. Lend it to other people at higher rate of interest than the bank pays on deposits. The difference should be enough to take care of the expenses ( salaries and establishment expenses ) and deliver a net profit. But in modern times, simple things get complicated. Governments start interfering with the banks’ working. Banks are made to give loans that are not viable and to the borrowers without good credentials. In India, we had Loan Melas in the time of Rajiv Gandhi’s government which was a brainchild of Janardhan Poojai, MOS Finance. Presently we have MUDRA loans. These type of loans along with the frauds like Nirav Modi or bad loans like Kingfisher Airlines, Jet Airways, Air India, Reliance Communication, Vodafone Idea, Bhushan Steel and many more sit heavily on the banks’ balance sheets. In the present state of affairs Bank Stocks in India are not a good long term investment. My answer is more specific to public sector banks. This a screen shot from my trades in February 2015: The two bank stock trades are highlighted. Five years ago, CANARA BANK was trading at a price of more than Rs. 440. On Friday, April 17,2020, the closing price is Rs. 86.85. The biggest public sector bank, State Bank of India shares were trading at a price higher than Rs. 300 five years ago. On Friday, April 17 the stock price went up considerably after the press briefing of RBI Governor and was quoted at Rs. 193.25. And five years is a considerably long period of time. The trend remains the same: If one keeps on doing same thing and expects different results, it would be foolishness. But our banks keep doing the same all the time. It is the chatter of the cheer leaders on the business channels who build the hype which makes the stock prices go up from time to time. People start believing that these stocks are good. Government rushes in and gives a dose of liquidity by way of recapitalization and more people buy these stocks to send the prices higher. That is when the smart money makes the exit and the general public is left holding the duds. A big injection of public funds was given to public sector banks in October 2017. Immediately the stock prices shot up. The gains were 25–50% in a single day as if all the problems of the sector were resolved. Then in August 2019, more money was given to these banks and 10 banks merged into 4. Let us look at the prices from October 2017 to present. I have not updated for April 17, 2020 but that is not going to be much different. Every one of these stocks have lost value in this period in spite of government putting in good money in these banks. Private Sector : We do not know who is hiding what. If there are few good performers like HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, AXISBANK and KOTAKBANK, we have YESBANK, RBLBANK and INDUSINDBANK which have performed extremely bad. The sector is troubled already. Troubles will not go away just by RBI relaxing the lending norms. In fact that will lead to more trouble in the future. To Conclude : Banking in present times is not the old sedate method of making money for the business and the stock holders. It is now a high risk business full of dubious decisions, encouraged by the governments and the regulators to take more risks in the name of ease of doing business. Others are enjoying that easing whereas banks bear the brunt of bad loans and defaults. The cycle will never stop because the banks are not being run as banks but money giving institutions without expectations of getting it back. This is a harsh conclusion but unfortunately true. Neither the banks or the government will accept this harsh truth but truth has a way of finally prevailing and it shows itself in the stock prices after some time. Banking stocks are not a good investment. These are my thoughts and views. Readers are welcome to differ. Thanks for reading.

Question: Does the seller always win in options trading?
Answer: Does the seller always win in Options Trading?: I have been away from Quora for more than a month now. This question brings me back. There are many myths propagated in the market like: (a) Option Buyers do not make money. (b) Only way to make money in Option Trading is by writing ( selling) options as time always works in favour of the seller. (c) Almost 80% of the Options expire worthless. All of these are part truths. The real truth is that Option Sellers make small profit regularly for a long time only to give it back and much more in just one day/one week or one month. Only their failures are not talked about. Talking about the failures of big traders and institutions is not fashionable. Those with very deep pockets survive and continue with their trades believing the same half truths. Others who just joined the selling band wagon lose their capital and do not come back to market for few years. The same cycle repeats. I know many readers will not believe what I have just stated till they actually live this horrible experience. I have seen people make Rs. 2–3 lakhs every month for three years and then lose Rs. 3.00 Crores in a single day. This trader was profitable for 36 months and failed only on a single day. The day was September 21, 2018 when NIFTY tanked 400 points from the high point of the day and then recovered 300 points from the low. I would not like to encounter such a day. I will illustrate with another example: This is a healthy goat in a goat farm. He gets good food every day. That good food is the regular consistent profit. The goat looks healthy like option sellers look profitable. Then comes the day when the goat is slaughtered. All that good food counts for nothing. Another goat replaces this one and gets same good food every day. Again it makes consistent small gains on daily basis till the day of slaughter. Many days of consistent profits with proof to show for it followed by just one day of loss. To me Option Selling is like being that goat. About 80% Options expiring worthless: I agree that this is close to being true. But nobody works out what was the pay off in the options which ended up in the money. I have been posting my trades on my blog for last 15 months. About 62% of trades have either expired worthless or lost money. But the successful trades have made a profit of about Rs. 800000 on a deployed capital of Rs. 200000. All the trades were Option Buying trades. The details can be read here: Review of Trades - 15 Months - May 2018 to July 2019 I have no reason to believe that the option seller always wins in option trading. To Summarize: An option buyer becomes an option seller just after buying the option. An option seller is a buyer immediately after selling. To make profit, both have to get their trades right. Theories and loosely stated words do not make money. It is a trader with a belief, a method and patience to wait in a good trade who makes money. All others count for the 90% losers. You are welcome to disagree with my views but these views are based on real life observations and many person to person talks with successful and unsuccessful traders. After all markets exist because of difference in views. Thanks for reading. Image Source : Google Images

Question: How do I avoid loss and earn consistently from stock markets?
Answer: How do I avoid loss and earn consistently from the stock market? : This quote by Warren Buffet is one of the most popular market quotes. It would be wonderful never to lose money. But trading life is not see easy. Losses visit far more frequently that we would like. There is no avoiding them. We do the next best thing. We keep the losses small. We trade with a defined stop loss. That way, the capital is preserved even when there are a few trades going wrong. And when a trade goes right, we try to take the maximum possible profit. We try to do so, it does not mean that we shall always get it. But taking small profits is not going to make one a consistent gainer. Such questions are repeated so often here on Quora that it is not possible to frame an answer every time. Answer: How do people whose only income is from stock market spend their entire day ? : Who are the people whose only income is from stock market? This will include day traders and stock market intermediaries ( brokers and their staff), consultants, advisers and our favorite experts on business channels. I do not know how these people spend their entire day. Every full time trader will have a different routine. I can talk about my typical day. Currently my only source of income is stock market. I trade ( not day trades , mostly positional trades in stock options) on the market days. I write answers on Quora mostly on stock market topics and at times dabble into politics and some other matters. I run a blog OptionsNext for sharing my views on Option Trading. Along with these activities I conduct Workshops on F&O Trading in various cities . In the year 2018, 400 participants have attended these workshops. All these activities are related to Stock Market. How the day is spent ? : Stock Market trading hours are from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm. This is the time I am in front of my desktop monitor watching the moves of my selected list of stocks along with NIFTY and BANK NIFTY. While watching, I do a lot of reading on Quora. I am a very slow trader taking just 15–20 trades in a month, so while viewing the market moves, I have a lot of reading time. In the same time I respond to comments on my blog and the e mails received regarding the F&O sessions. There is some work to be done before the market opens. From 7:30 am to 8:30 am is the time for writing my blog post for the day and writing my Quora answers. I try to stick to this time table on most days, but there are exceptions too like I am writing this answer during trading hours. After 3:30 it is time for a little rest. Then there is a second session in the evening between 7:00 pm to 8:30 pm to read the financial news of the day, to plan for the blog post for next day, to respond to new messages and mails etc. This is how my typical day is spent. On weekends, I meet some of my Quora followers/ people who attended my programs and want further discussions etc and this takes about 3–4 hours. Preparation for the F&O workshops also takes some of my time on weekends. Other than that I do a lot of reading ( mostly fiction about 2–3 hours a day ) and somehow find time for that. So this was how I spend my entire day. Not exactly like going to office but not very different either. Once the trading hours are over, I do not bother as to what is likely to happen tomorrow. There is no point worrying about what we do not and can not control. I enjoy my trading, my reading, my writing and interaction with other traders. And when some good profits come in, that makes my day. Thanks for reading.

Question: Will the Indian stock market crash to 10000 NIFTY in January 2019?
Answer: Will the Indian Stock Market Crash to 10000 NIFTY in January 2019 ? : Predictions, speculation, analysis of the market moves is something every market participant indulges in. Sometime we are proved right and we tell it to all the world. Most of the time we are wrong and we do not talk about it. I have been looking for a crash since last two years but it is not coming. Why me, there are world renowned experts who are predicting a crash but again it is not coming. Experts had predicted a crash when Brexit happened. They had predicted a crash if Donald Trump was elected US president. both the events happened and the markets moved on and continued to make new highs. This is what NIFTY has done over last 5 years. It was subdued after making the then all time high in March 2015 ( 9119 on march 04, 2015) till end of February 2016. From then on it has not looked back. I agree that it is down from the August 2018 highs of 11760 by little more than 1000 points but it can not be termed as a crash. Whether a crash is coming ? : I wish I knew. I wish I could read the tea leaves. And time it to perfection like 10000 in January 2019. It may happen if our market did just what happened in US market in the last few days. Still, it would not be called a crash. That would just replicate the status of previous year. The recent 52 week low was 9951 ( on March 23, 2018) . So the 10000 level would be higher than that and if an Index has not breached the previous 52 week low, we do not call it a crash. It may qualify as a correction but surely not a crash. What do we want to do with the prediction of a crash ? : If the aim is to make money from the impending crash, just buy deep out of money PUT options of NIFTY and BANK NIFTY. You win if the crash happens. You lose the premium paid if things go the other way. If owning a large portfolio, hedge with some appropriate PUT options so as to stay protected. A good part of the portfolio should be covered by this method. If none of the above is the case, just watch the business channels. Lot of guys do this stuff everyday and are proven wrong almost everyday. Well, my personal view— NIFTY may go down from current levels but 10000 may hold till the Finance Minister presents another dumb budget like in 2018. That would be the time to go below 10000. I have been wrong in the past and maybe wrong again in the future. It happens all the time. Like Jesse Livermore so aptly said about most of the people most of the time. Enjoy the market roller coaster. Thanks for reading. Images : Google Images and Fyers Web

Question: As a non Malayali, which was the first Malayalam movie you have seen? Can you share your experience watching it?
Answer: My first Malayalam movie: The year was 1989. I was posted at Lower Periyar Dam Project of Kerala State Electricity Board. My posting at the project was not for a long duration but I enjoyed my brief stay in Kerala. The place of residence was Kothamangalam, a very nice small town. Well, I had become little conversant with Telugu, Tamil and Kannada because of my previous postings and friends in those days. Malayalam was still a mystery. My children began their schooling at Kothamangalam and I became familiar with the alphabets. More of the language came to me through interactions with workers at the construction site. Those were the days of VHS cassettes and VCRs. One could rent a cassette of a movie for a day and watch with a VCP/VCR. I have still got one VCP lying around, most likely non functional as it is unused since the year 2001. That is enough introduction. My boss told that he has rented a cassette for the day and both our families can watch the movie together. He was from Tamil Nadu but could understand Malayalam. For me, it was okay. I had watched Telugu, Tamil and Kannada movies too without knowing the languages. No harm in experimenting again. The movie was: CHEPPU —- A Priyadarshan movie starring Mohanlal in the lead role. The movie was based on the theme of college politics, drugs and violence. Mohanlal played the role of an upright college teacher. I could see the intensity of expressions but the dialogues were beyond me. Helpful explanations from my boss did not help much. Mostly in similar themed movies, hero emerges triumphant in the climax. This movie was different. Hero died. That was poignant and the reason I remember the movie. I understand that it was a big hit too. I did not watch any other Malayalam movie till yesterday. This time it is DRISHYAM 2. Once again it is Mohanlal who carries the film. Cheppu was made in 1987. Mohanlal was the top actor along with Mammootty. We are in 2021 and Mohanlal is still going strong. Just like fine matured wine. This time I was helped by English subtitles. This was my experience with my first Malayalam movie. Thanks for reading. Question: Is it a good time to invest in stocks of PSU banks in India? BOB, SBI or any other stocks you can recommend. Investment horizon is for long term.
Answer: Is it a good time to invest in stocks of PSU banks in India? : This question was posted here sometime in the year 2016. We are now in April 2020. Markets have seen multiple all time highs and given up significantly over last 3 months due to COVID -19 spread throughout the world. Let us revisit the question in the present time. How the PSU Banks performed recently?: Let us review some details over last 2–3 years. On October 24, 2017 , then then Finance Minister Arun Jaitley made a televised announcement about recapitalization of Public Sector Banks. Announcement came just 10 minutes before the market close. There was some positive move immediately but the big move was to come next day. Most of the PSU Bank stocks went up 30-60% next day. A great day for these stocks. People were lapping up the stocks as if they found the key to Midas Gold. What happened next?: Stock market is a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term. It weighed, separated the grain from the chaff and told us that mostly it was chaff only. There was more recapitalization, relaxation of norms by the RBI and another set of mergers announced by the present Finance Minister in August 2019. Merging three bad banks does not make one good bank. But market players never learn. They rush in to buy these duds whereas the real smart people take this opportunity to sell the worthless stock to all who are willing to buy. Let us have a look at how these stocks went up in a day in October 2017 and where they sit currently. NIFTY has declined 11.5% in this period. Among these PSU Banks, SBI is the stock with minimum loss which is 42.21%. There are 6 stocks which have lost more than 80% of the value. Who needs Nirav Modi and who needs a fraud to get money from these banks? Just go short on these stocks and make money. Unfortunately, many of them are not in F&O segment. In that case, do not invest in them and save money. Conclusion : Throwing good money after bad does not work even if the money belongs to Government. A bad business remains a bad business unless the business practices change. There maybe some rebound at some stage but these stocks remain on the AVOID list. Question: Rahul has demanded JPC probe into Stock market scam blaming Modi, Shah and FM behind it as investors have lost 30 lakh crores. What is your opinion on this?
Answer: Stock Market Scam: I have been a keen follower of electoral politics since 1977 when Congress went out of power for the first time at the national level. I have been a stock market learner too from the same year. This question combines both the fields, so I am tempted to answer. What happened over last 1 week?: Markets were uncertain before the Lok Sabha elections concluded. There were talks of 400 + seats for NDA and towards the end of the long drawn out elections, there was some fatigue in that theme and in the market too. Most people, including the stock market players believed that BJP would get a majority, a decent majority on its own to form the government for a third consecutive term. Exit polls by various TV channels added to that belief. Home Minister Amit Shah told in some election rally that markets are bound to go up after the BJP/NDA victory. So the smart investor should invest in the market. (Not these exact words but something along the same theme) Exit polls happened on June 01, Saturday and market went through the roof on June 03, Monday. On June 04, as the results were pouring in and BJP was not getting the anticipated results, market euphoria of Monday turned into despair (it happens quite regularly in the market) and the index crashed in a big way. This is what made Rahul Gandhi say that investors lost Rs. 30 lakh crores. Did they actually lose?: Some traders surely lost in a big way as their positions built over previous few days went into a tailspin and losses had to be booked. Trading is such a beast. It devours profits and turns them into a loss in no time. But then, traders knew the risks. As things settled down, it became clear that BJP is coming back to power as NDA for the third term, market recovered and by Friday, June 07, 2024 had made another record high for both NIFTY and SENSEX. See how it happened: Where did the investor lose money? Those who stayed put for 2–3 days, recouped whatever notional loss was there. There was no loss of Rs. 30 lakh crores to investors as claimed by Rahul Gandhi. Why did Rahul Gandhi say it?: Mostly politicians make false statements and accusations on each other. This is common to all parties. Rahul Gandhi in his new found confidence after improved results in the elections, probably thought that he has got another strong point against Modi- Shah. He will have to look elsewhere for any strong point. This point is not worth a small debate, what to speak of a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Why should we waste public money in useless discussions which are bound to result in nothing. Was Amit Shah wrong in speaking about stock market in his election speech?: Maybe, to a very small extent. But then election speeches are all bluster and rhetoric. Nobody actually means what they speak. We had lot of other nonsense like Mangalsutra, Buffaloes, Khata Khat, Cash in Tempos . If public can see through all that, why would they bother about what Amit Shah says about stock market. Yes, few people lost money: So what. These people are not the poor people who need hand holding by the government or opposition leaders. They took an investment/trading decision based on their reading of the market. It went wrong and the money was lost. It happens everyday to the traders in stock market. Neither Mr. Modi nor Rahul Gandhi care for these traders. It was just to score a point over Modi-Shah, which did not amount to much. To Conclude: Market has a mind of its own. It reacts to political events in a volatile manner but eventually everything evens out. Yesterday, oath taking and ministry formation was done. This is the market reaction today: Today also, NIFTY index made a new record high at 23411.90 and then climbed down from that level. Highs and lows are daily occurrences in the market. Only the volatility is very high on election results kind of days. On Saturday, June 08, I had written this answer: Pramod Kumar's answer to Why is Congress happy despite the loss? Excerpt from that answer: There is nothing to be inquired into. No wrongs have been committed. Rahul Gandhi should focus on things other than stock market. Market will go higher or lower without interference from the politicians. Occasional positive nudges are okay for the market but nothing more is needed. These were my views on the question posed. Thanks for reading.
